Ask before extracting when an archive would unpack to a much larger size (at least 1 GB and over 500× its packed size, or 1 TB or more). This might be a compression bomb, or a legitimate large file such as a virtual machine disk image.

In archives created on macOS, the __MACOSX folder, .DS_Store, and files starting with ._ aren't needed on Windows. When enabled, they are skipped during extraction and ignored by the single-folder check.

When an archive is damaged or incomplete, keep whatever data could be extracted (images, videos, and text files are often still partially usable). Files with errors are listed when done. When off, corrupted files are deleted. Wrong passwords, canceled tasks, or full disks always delete incomplete files.
Ask once when "Delete archive" is selected on the archive at the top of the folder tree (it moves to the Recycle Bin). When off, the archive is deleted immediately and you return to the home page.
Ask before deleting items from an archive
Ask once when Delete is pressed or "Delete" is selected. Items are removed directly from the archive. They don't go to the Recycle Bin and can't be restored (unless the backup below is on).
Keep a backup when an archive is changed
When files in an archive are added, deleted, renamed, or edited, keep the archive as it was in the same folder (with .bak added to the name). Each change overwrites the previous backup.

The app used by "Edit" in the context menu. When empty, text files open in Notepad and other files open in their default app. Full paths are supported (e.g., C:\\Program Files\\Notepad++\\notepad++.exe).
Ask before updating edited files in the archive
After saving an edited file, ask whether to update it in the archive. When off, it's updated automatically.
Warn before opening programs, installers, and scripts
Ask for confirmation when double-clicking an executable file (.exe, .msi, .bat, etc.) inside an archive.
What to extract when opening a program
Programs often need files in the same folder (DLLs, data files). "Same folder" extracts the folder, including subfolders, to a temporary folder before running the program.
Close the window automatically after a context-menu action
When you extract or compress from the context menu, close the small window automatically after everything succeeds. Turn this off to keep the window open and see the result.

After compressing, read the new archive to make sure it's intact.

The layout selected in the View menu (details / list / icons) is used the next time an archive is opened. When on, "Default view" below follows your last choice.
Details shows columns and supports sorting. List is the most compact. Icons shows large icons. You can switch at any time from the View menu.

Single level shows one folder at a time; use the folder tree on the left or the path bar to navigate. "List all" shows the files from all levels in one list. You can switch at any time from the toolbar.
Use File Explorer icons for files and folders in the list and folder tree (based on installed apps). When off, LycanZip uses its own colored icons.
Applies to non-solid archives only (reading one image from a solid archive requires decoding the data before it, so no thumbnails are made). Read in the background only when needed.

Preload nearby images in the background for faster paging. This sets the maximum memory used for preloaded images. When off, images are loaded on demand.
Register LycanZip as an archive app
Once registered, LycanZip appears in "Open with" and "Default apps". Windows requires you to set default apps manually in System Settings.

Files: add to archive, compress to ZIP / 7z, and more. Archives: open, extract, test, preview, and more. Affects only the current user and can be turned off at any time. On Windows 11, it appears under "Show more options".

Shown at the top level of the Windows 11 context menu, without selecting "Show more options". Requires a signed menu package. Affects only the current user and can be turned off at any time. The entries are the same as in the menu above, and both can be on at once.
